title: She Crawled Across a Flooded Bridge to Stop a Train #shorts
description:
July 6, 1881, Honey Creek, Iowa. A locomotive crashes through a storm-wrecked bridge, and a passenger train is due at midnight. A teenage girl crawls across the Des Moines River bridge in the dark to stop it.

Sources: Library of Congress, print of Kate Shelley and the railroad disaster of July 6, 1881 - https://www.loc.gov/item/95512234/ ; Wikipedia, "Kate Shelley" - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Shelley
Narration voiced with AI. Animation made by the channel.

title: A 60-Foot Wall of Water Hit This Town in 1889 #shorts
description:
May 31, 1889. The South Fork Dam fails 14 miles above Johnstown, Pennsylvania. 57 minutes later, a wall of water and wreckage hits the town. 2,208 people died - still the deadliest flash flood in U.S. history.

Sources: National Park Service, Johnstown Flood National Memorial - https://www.nps.gov/jofl/learn/historyculture/index.htm ; Wikipedia, "Johnstown Flood" - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnstown_Flood
Narration voiced with AI. Animation made by the channel.

title: The Fever That Emptied America's Capital (1793) #shorts
description:
August 1793, Philadelphia - then the U.S. capital. A fever turns skin yellow and kills within days. 20,000 people flee, even President Washington. The real killer: mosquitoes.

Sources: Library of Congress, "The 1793 Yellow Fever Epidemic: The Washingtons, Hamilton and Jefferson" - https://blogs.loc.gov/loc/2020/05/the-1793-yellow-fever-epidemic-the-washingtons-hamilton-and-jefferson/ ; Absalom Jones and Richard Allen, "A narrative of the proceedings of the black people, during the late awful calamity in Philadelphia" (1794), Library of Congress - https://www.loc.gov/item/02013737/ ; Wikipedia, "1793 Philadelphia yellow fever epidemic" - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1793_Philadelphia_yellow_fever_epidemic
Narration voiced with AI. Animation made by the channel.

title: Trapped Underground for 14 Days (1925) #shorts
description:
January 30, 1925. Floyd Collins gets pinned by a rock deep in Sand Cave, Kentucky. The rescue becomes one of the first huge news stories on American radio.

Sources: Wikipedia, "Floyd Collins" - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floyd_Collins ; Library of Congress, Chronicling America, The Citizen-Times (Scottsville, Ky.), February 19, 1925 - https://www.loc.gov/item/sn86069484/1925-02-19/ed-1/
